decision: Each MCP server in the Codex user config.toml is disabled by name with -c mcp_servers.<name>.enabled=false.
rationale: codex app-server has no --ignore-user-config, and -c mcp_servers={} does not clear servers from the user's config.toml, so only per-name disabling removes them. Implemented in codex/protocol.py _user_mcp_overrides.
alternatives_considered: -c mcp_servers={} (does not clear user servers)
--ignore-user-config (not supported by app-server)

decision: A Codex config.toml that exists but cannot be read or parsed fails the call with CliProtocolError naming the path; a missing file is fine.
rationale: Codex would still load that file, so its MCP servers could not be disabled by name; failing is the only way to avoid running without isolation.

decision: Codex token usage is the sum of tokenUsage.last over every thread/tokenUsage/updated event in a turn.
rationale: tokenUsage.last is per model call, not per turn, so a turn with several model calls would otherwise report only the final call.
alternatives_considered: Report only the last event's usage (undercounts multi-call turns)

decision: Token metrics mean the same for both models: input_tokens includes cached tokens, cache_read_tokens is the cached part, cache_write_tokens is Claude cache creation, and total_tokens is input_tokens + output_tokens.
rationale: Identical semantics let callers compare cost across Claude Code and Codex; CLI overhead is tens of thousands of mostly cached input tokens per call, so compare on total tokens.

decision: Failures are typed: CliTimeoutError (504) and CliProtocolError (502) subclass ModelProviderError, and rate limits and context overflow raise Agno's own ModelRateLimitError and ContextWindowExceededError.
rationale: Reusing Agno's classes lets Agno's FallbackConfig(on_rate_limit=...) and callers react without knowing this package.
alternatives_considered: Package-specific rate limit and context classes (would break FallbackConfig)

decision: Child CLI processes never see ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL, CODEX_API_KEY, CLAUDECODE or CLAUDE_* variables except CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT; for Claude they are blanked, for Codex they are removed.
rationale: A CLI must never fall back to API billing or another endpoint by accident. The Claude Agent SDK merges the parent environment and cannot delete keys, so empty values hide them; Codex is spawned by this package, so it gets a clean environment.

decision: The CLI session id (Claude session or Codex thread) is stored in provider_data on assistant messages.
rationale: Agno's own history then persists it, so a new agent instance with the same session_id resumes the CLI session (with add_history_to_context=True).
session_context: Seeded at ReasonHold adoption from README.md and the code; approved by the maintainer.

decision: When a stored CLI session no longer exists, the model logs a warning, starts a new CLI session with the Agno history replayed as a transcript, and stores the new session id.
rationale: Session files get cleaned up or the Agno session moves machines. Codex retries only on a thread/resume error reply; Claude's SDK reports a missing session only as a failed process, so Claude retries when resuming fails before the session starts, except on rate limits or context overflow.
session_context: Seeded at ReasonHold adoption from README.md and the code; approved by the maintainer.

decision: Tools with requires_confirmation pause the Agno run: Claude defers the call with a PreToolUse hook and resumes the session; Codex declines the pending call, interrupts the turn and resumes the thread on continue_run.
rationale: A rejected tool never runs and a confirmed tool runs exactly once. Codex server requests are answered by method: command and file-change approvals and MCP elicitation are declined, anything else gets a JSON-RPC error.
session_context: Seeded at ReasonHold adoption from README.md and the code; approved by the maintainer.

decision: Codex structured output uses the OpenAI strict schema variant (every property required, no extra properties, formerly optional properties made nullable, property names never stripped), and structured output is parsed only on the non-stream path.
rationale: Codex requires a strict schema; property names that look like schema keywords are field names and must survive. Stream mode stores concatenated deltas, so parsing happens only on the non-stream final answer.

A missing or unreadable skills directory gives no entries, because Codex cannot read it either.

Only the /root delegation prompt is blanked; Codex's <multi_agent_mode> 'do not spawn unless asked' line is kept on purpose.

Only a patched model_catalog_json removed them (turn 5), which depends on the format of models_cache.json and pins model metadata, against the package's premise of running the real CLI as installed. With the tools still offered, <multi_agent_mode> is the only instruction against spawning, so blanking it would make spawns more likely. Maintainer's choice, 2026-10-01. Whether a sub-agent can call the caller's Agno tools has not been tested.

Patched model_catalog_json, opt-in
Fail the call with CliProtocolError when a spawn is seen (keeps the CLI as installed; not chosen)
wait_agent_enabled=false and max_concurrent_threads_per_session=1 as a cap (does not stop a spawn; not shipped, so nothing suggests a guard that does not exist)

decision: The built-in Codex provider's stream settings cannot be changed: codex app-server (codex-cli 0.155.1) refuses to start when any model_providers.openai key is set, so the package keeps Codex's defaults (stream_idle_timeout_ms 300000, stream_max_retries 5, request_max_retries 4) and does not define a custom copy of the provider; a Codex reconnect is visible as an app-server error notification with willRetry true and codexErrorInfo.responseStreamDisconnected, which TurnTracker already ignores.
rationale: Measured in reports/2026-10-01-substrate-checks.md. The error is 'model_providers contains reserved built-in provider IDs: openai. Built-in providers cannot be overridden' (exit 1, with or without --strict-config). The defaults come from codex-rs/model-provider-info for v0.155.1. Codex's own reconnect therefore waits 300 s, equal to Sendesis's Codex wall clock, which is why stalls cost about 300 s. A custom provider (base_url https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, wire_api responses, requires_openai_auth true) authenticated with the ChatGPT login, and with stream_idle_timeout_ms 300 it produced 'Reconnecting... 1/1' (willRetry true), then a final error (willRetry false), thread status systemError and a failed turn. That route is not adopted: it copies the built-in provider's definition into the package, which a Codex release can change, and the package-side idle limit does not need it.
alternatives_considered: -c model_providers.openai.stream_idle_timeout_ms (rejected by Codex: app-server exits 1)
A custom provider copy with a shorter stream_idle_timeout_ms (works, but copies Codex's provider definition into the package)

decision: For Claude Code 2.1.287 with claude-opus-5-5 at effort high, the Claude idle default is 60 s, measured on every SDK message after init, and it holds only with include_partial_messages on: when idle_timeout_s is set, ClaudeCodeModel requests partial messages whatever the caller's stream mode, and counts the deltas for the idle clock without yielding them to a non-streaming caller.
rationale: 14 healthy runs, all at effort high (reports/2026-10-01-substrate-checks.md, raw data in reports/2026-10-01-substrate-checks-claude.jsonl). Shapes: Sendesis-style review with tools and schema, puzzle, essay, long-think. In stream mode the longest gap after init was 5.55 s (tool result to the next message_start). Gaps inside thinking were at most 1.65 s, because the CLI sends system:thinking_tokens every 1.2-1.7 s even in non-stream mode, and gaps inside text deltas at most 0.14 s. In non-stream mode the whole answer arrives as one message, so the gap grows with answer length (37.5 s for about 1200 words), and no fixed idle limit is safe without partial messages. The pre-registered margin rule (2 x max stream gap, rounded up to 30 s, floor 60 s) gives 60 s. Limits: the longest thinking stretch observed was 18 s; the CLI's own API backoff, slow tools and rate-limit waits were not observed. Re-measure with tools/measure_cadence.py when the CLI version, model or effort changes.
alternatives_considered: Keep the Claude default at None (the request's interim position; the data now supports a value)
An idle limit on whole SDK messages in non-stream mode (trips on long answers: 37.5 s for about 1200 words)
A default set by analogy with Codex's 60 s (refused by the Sendesis stall design; this one comes from Claude measurements)
